chapter: Piron, Clarence Williams and the ODJB repertoire
title: Correcting the dates of the colored-melody numbers and novelty singing
summary: The interviewer and La Rocca settle that the tunes were popular around 1918, played as novelties even in London, and La Rocca says he sang Margie before it was published.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: You want me to read the part of it? Now you were going to correct that date back there. You said 1819, and that just couldn't be right. 1918. That was 1918. And this was the years the tunes were popular that you were talking about. You were saying these colored melodies.
You were playing the brown scale, who you fought?
It started around 1819. And when did it last? 1918. You see, 1819. It started around.
I got a role too. We played them all the way through London. They weren't in all.

We played the same pieces through London. Wherever we went, we played them. As dance tunes, you know? We used them as novelties. I see. Along with our other novelists, we had, you couldn't just give them dry music all the time. You got out there, you did a little humming and singing. I sang Margie before it was even published and made a hit out of it. I haven't got no voice. Is it recording now?
